## Dagger

Observed evidence:

- `ComponentProcessor` is a Javac annotation processor with `@AutoService` and an isolating incremental-processor declaration (`dagger-ComponentProcessor.java:36-42`).
- The outer processor owns a delegate instance and delegates initialization/processing (`:82-100`, `:117-129`).
- `DelegateComponentProcessor` declares injected registries, generators, processing steps, plugins, caches, and options (`dagger-DelegateComponentProcessor.java:79-86`).
- A generated `DaggerDelegateComponentProcessor_Injector` creates and injects the processor (`:112-114`).
- The injector explicitly lists component modules and uses a `@Component.Factory` with bound runtime inputs (`:139-163`).
- Plugins are supplied by tests or loaded through `ServiceLoaders` (`:88-116`).
- Processing has round lifecycle hooks, source generation, plugin finalization, and per-round cache clearing (`:119-137`).
- Legacy plugins on KSP emit an error but processing continues for the remainder of the round (`:97-110`).

Transferable lesson: generated, typed internal wiring is a real industry pattern. Get Modular can use a private finite emitter to wire its own cohesive compiler features, provided the selected plan demonstrably controls the actual factories.

Must reject: Java annotation identity as portable module identity; `AutoService`/`ServiceLoader` discovery; runtime plugin registries; Dagger cache lifetimes; and continue-after-error behavior. Get Modular requires serializable identities, explicit bindings, no executable discovery, and bounded fail-closed diagnostics. This boundary is stated explicitly in ADR-0008 (`docs/decisions/0008-bounded-internal-engine-self-composition.md:447-451`) and GM-REQ-001/002/006/010-014.

Unverified from these files: artifact upgrades, process isolation, portable compatibility, or unload semantics. The only cleanup observed is plugin finalization and cache clearing, not module unload.

## Bazel

Observed evidence:

- `compile.sh` defines a finite bootstrap: build a seed without Bazel or accept a supplied previous Bazel, then use it to build `src:bazel_nojdk`, copying the result to `output/bazel` (`compile.sh:17-21`, `:42-76`).
- Bootstrap configuration uses `/dev/null` as the default bazelrc, standalone actions, explicit toolchains, repository/output roots, and direct-dependency checking (`bootstrap.sh:23-59`).
- The scratch compiler explicitly compiles annotation processors before “enough of Bazel” (`bootstrap-compile.sh:291-295`).
- Developer checkouts lack generated protobuf output; bootstrap therefore requires a distribution artifact or explicit `protoc` and gRPC plugin (`bootstrap-compile.sh:223-289`).
- The script creates embedded tools, deploy JARs, install bases, output bases, and user roots (`:303-373`, `:413-437`).
- It propagates essentially all environment variables into the bootstrapped Bazel invocation (`:396-410`).
- The bootstrap sets `--lockfile_mode=update` (`bootstrap.sh:46-49`).

Transferable lesson: use a finite, explicitly staged bootstrap with named outputs and explicit toolchain/dependency inputs. Keep the graph acyclic and stop after the required stage comparison.

Must reject:

- A previous released binary or distribution archive as Get Modular’s authoritative seed. ADR-0008 requires current-source stage0 and says a previous release is not a required seed (`ADR-0008:93-98`, `:212-219`).
- Mutable lockfiles and broad environment propagation as evidence of hermeticity.
- Distribution-generated sources as an implicit dependency.
- Bazel’s much larger bootstrap/toolchain surface for the Core runtime.

Bazel provides no evidence of module unload or portable capability compatibility. Failures are shell-level (`set -o errexit` and explicit `fail` paths), not a bounded diagnostic contract. Missing generated sources/tools are hard bootstrap failures (`bootstrap-compile.sh:246-289`).

## Gradle

Observed evidence:

- Root settings include three separate build-logic builds: `build-logic-settings`, `build-logic-commons`, and `build-logic` (`settings.gradle.kts:8-26`).
- The root DSL groups hundreds of projects into coarse-grained `module`, `platform`, `subproject`, and `uses` relationships (`:30-38`, `:182-208`, `:244-306`).
- `build-logic-settings` separates root lifecycle, dependency data, special-purpose plugins, and an explicitly named `kotlin-dsl-shared-runtime` that is shipped in the distribution (`build-logic-settings.gradle.kts:39-69`).
- `build-logic-commons` is another layer with shared basics, dependency platforms, module identity, quality rules, plugin-building, and publishing (`build-logic-commons-settings.gradle.kts:32-55`).
- The architecture diagram is generated from the settings authority rather than being hand-maintained (`platforms.md:1-12`, `:126-133`).
- Platform dependencies are explicit (`software uses core`, `jvm uses core and software`, etc.; `settings.gradle.kts:207-248`).

Transferable lesson: keep build-only logic in a separate layered DAG; use coarse cohesive groupings; make cross-layer edges explicit; generate navigation/architecture views from the same declarations.

Must reject:

- Treating the large root settings file as a portable identity registry.
- Turning every product feature into a build plugin.
- Using plugin IDs, project names, repository selection, or feature-preview state as Get Modular compatibility semantics.
- Treating settings/include order as business ordering.

These files provide no evidence for runtime unload, structured error behavior, or hermetic builds. They show build composition, not runtime activation.

## Transferable rules

| Rule | Confidence | Conditions |
|---|---:|---|
| Use a finite `stage0 → plan → emitter → stage1` DAG. | 9/10 | Build-time only; no per-call bootstrap or unbounded fixed-point loop. |
| Make generated wiring disposable derived output. | 9/10 | Authority remains declarations, profile, allowlist, emitter, and input manifest; compare exact bytes. |
| Separate private build logic from runtime Core code. | 9/10 | Explicitly audit any runtime-shipped exception. |
| Keep identity/declaration ownership with each feature. | 9/10 | Generated inventories/diagrams are navigation only, never a second registry. |
| Define ordering explicitly. | 9/10 | Use profile order and deterministic graph ordering; never registration, filesystem, locale, or discovery order. |
| Keep lifecycle and operational authority outside Get Modular. | 10/10 | Product host owns loading, activation, routing, drain, recovery, retirement, and unload. |
| Use closed compatibility and bounded diagnostics. | 10/10 | Exact serializable compatibility tokens; invalid worlds fail before factories. |
| Isolate stage outputs/caches and pin all inputs. | 8/10 | Fresh roots, poisoned-output tests, no network, environment allowlist, lockfile/toolchain/source manifest. |
| Recover by exact source/toolchain revert and cold regeneration. | 9/10 | Never silently publish stage0 as stage1 or restore generated wiring as authority. |

## Anti-patterns

- `ServiceLoader` or ambient discovery deciding providers.
- Framework annotations, class names, Bazel labels, or Gradle project names used as portable module identity.
- A prior binary, mutable lockfile, or ambient environment silently influencing qualification.
- One central registry/settings file becoming the owner of every feature identity.
- Runtime containers, unload, hot replacement, or per-request graph construction inside the composition core.
- Assuming `P0 = P1` proves correctness when both stages share the same bug; independent vectors remain mandatory.
- Comparing a generated file with itself or allowing stale outputs/caches into qualification.

ADR-0008 itself records the central limitation: the industry review supports bounded generated composition only conditionally, and remains review evidence rather than implementation proof (`ADR-0008:430-445`).
